issues.legal_issue: Police investigation of an alleged cognizable offence ordinarily proceeds without judicial interference, and the power to quash criminal proceedings is exercised sparingly in exceptional cases.
material_facts: A complainant lodged a first information report alleging forgery, fabrication of a company resolution, and fraudulent sale of company property.
The accused sought quashing while the police investigation was ongoing.
The appeal concerned an interim direction restricting action against the accused, not the merits of the allegations in the first information report.
issues.conclusion: The police have a statutory right and duty to investigate cognizable offences. Courts ordinarily must allow the investigation to proceed and may quash proceedings only sparingly, within the established exceptional categories; they must not assess the reliability of the allegations at the investigation stage.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 154 and 156 of Chapter XIV of the Code of Criminal Procedure confer the statutory framework for recording information and investigating cognizable offences. Section 482 CrPC and Article 226 of the Constitution permit intervention to prevent abuse of process or secure the ends of justice, but not arbitrary intervention or routine assessment of the merits during an incomplete investigation. The Court applied the principles in King-Emperor v. Khwaja Nazir Ahmad, R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab, State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, State of A.P. v. Golconda Linga Swamy, and State of Telangana v. Habib Abdullah Jeelani, among other authorities.

predicates.cognizable_offence_reported: A complainant reported alleged conduct that provides a basis to suspect a cognizable offence.
predicates.investigation_underway: Police had begun investigating the reported conduct and had not completed their evidence-gathering.
predicates.quashing_petition_pending: The accused sought to terminate the criminal proceedings while the investigation was ongoing.

issues.definition: When a cognizable offence is reported and an investigation is underway during a pending quashing proceeding, the investigation ordinarily proceeds unless an exceptional ground for quashing is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A court may stay further investigation while a quashing petition is pending only exceptionally, after applying the quashing standards and giving brief reasons that show its consideration of the relevant facts.
material_facts: The accused filed a petition to quash the first information report while the investigation was pending.
The High Court issued an interim direction concerning action against the accused while adjourning the quashing petition.
The judgment recognized that the facts may be incomplete or hazy at an early stage of investigation and that an interim stay can impede the investigation.
issues.conclusion: An interim stay of investigation is possible in an exceptional case, but must not be granted routinely or mechanically. The court must apply the parameters governing quashing and give brief reasons showing application of mind; where the facts are hazy and the investigation has just begun, the court should ordinarily allow the investigation to continue.
issues.legal_principle: The standards governing quashing under Section 482 CrPC and Article 226 apply to interim orders in quashing proceedings. The Court relied on R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab, State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, Imtiyaz Ahmad v. State of Uttar Pradesh, and Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited v. Central Bureau of Investigation. A reasoned order is required, and a stay must be exceptional rather than a means of delaying investigation or impairing access to justice.

rule.if: quashing_petition_pending and exceptional_ground_apparent and quashing_parameters_applied and brief_reasons_recorded

predicates.quashing_petition_pending: An accused has asked a court to quash criminal proceedings and that request remains pending.
predicates.exceptional_ground_apparent: The circumstances disclose an exceptional basis for concluding that interim interference is warranted under the standards for quashing proceedings.
predicates.quashing_parameters_applied: The court has considered the standards governing quashing and the relevant circumstances of the case.
predicates.brief_reasons_recorded: The court has stated brief reasons explaining why interim interference is warranted.

issues.definition: An interim stay may be granted when a quashing petition is pending, an exceptional ground is apparent, the court applies the quashing standards, and it records brief reasons.

issues.legal_issue: A blanket direction barring coercive measures during a pending quashing petition is unsustainable when it is unexplained, unclear in scope, or impedes the investigation.
material_facts: The High Court directed that no coercive measures be taken against the accused in relation to the first information report.
The direction gave no reasons and did not explain what measures it covered.
The police were investigating alleged cognizable offences, and the accused already had interim protection from arrest in a separate anticipatory-bail proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s blanket direction was unsustainable and was set aside because it was unexplained, unclear, and capable of impeding the police investigation and its statutory functions.
issues.legal_principle: An interim order granting extraordinary protection must state brief reasons that show application of mind and allow review by a higher forum. A direction against coercive measures must also clarify its scope. The Court relied on State of Telangana v. Habib Abdullah Jeelani, Special Director v. Mohd. Ghulam Ghouse, Nitco Tiles Ltd. v. Gujarat Ceramic Floor Tiles Mfg. Association, Hindustan Times Limited v. Union of India, and Kranti Associates (P) Ltd. v. Masood Ahmed.

rule.if: quashing_petition_pending and blanket_no_coercive_direction and (reasons_absent or direction_scope_unclear or investigation_right_impeded)

predicates.quashing_petition_pending: An accused has asked a court to quash criminal proceedings and that request remains pending.
predicates.blanket_no_coercive_direction: The court has directed generally that no coercive measures be taken against the accused in relation to the reported offence.
predicates.reasons_absent: The court has given no reasons for issuing the direction.
predicates.direction_scope_unclear: The direction does not identify what actions or measures it covers.
predicates.investigation_right_impeded: The direction restricts or may restrict police work in investigating the reported offence.

issues.definition: A blanket no-coercive-measures direction during a pending quashing petition is invalid if it lacks reasons, has unclear scope, or impedes the investigation.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot, after dismissing or declining to entertain a quashing petition, direct that the accused not be arrested during the investigation or until the final report is filed.
material_facts: The Court considered the practice of courts issuing protection from arrest while dismissing or otherwise not entertaining quashing petitions.
The judgment explained that an accused who apprehends arrest may apply for anticipatory bail before the competent court.
issues.conclusion: A direction not to arrest, or to take no coercive steps, during the investigation or until the final report is filed is impermissible when the quashing petition has been dismissed, disposed of, or not entertained.
issues.legal_principle: A post-dismissal direction against arrest effectively grants anticipatory-bail protection without applying the statutory conditions for that relief. The Court applied Section 438 CrPC and Section 482 CrPC and Article 226 of the Constitution, relying particularly on State of Telangana v. Habib Abdullah Jeelani and Ravuri Krishna Murthy v. State of Telangana.

predicates.quashing_petition_rejected_or_not_entert: A court has dismissed, disposed of, or declined to entertain an accused person's request to quash criminal proceedings.
predicates.arrest_protection_ordered_during_investi: The court has directed that the accused not be arrested, or that no coercive steps be taken, while the investigation continues.

issues.definition: When a quashing petition is rejected or not entertained, a direction protecting the accused from arrest during the investigation is impermissible.

issues.legal_issue: An application seeking action for alleged suppression of documents need not be entertained where the underlying quashing petition remains undecided and the alleged suppression would not affect the interim order under challenge.
material_facts: The accused applied for action under Section 340 read with Section 195(1)(b) CrPC, alleging that the complainant had suppressed documents and facts.
The underlying quashing petition remained for decision by the High Court.
The Supreme Court stated that the alleged documents would not have affected the reasons for its interim order.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to examine the merits of the suppression allegations, closed the application, and disposed of it.
issues.legal_principle: The application invoked Section 340 read with Section 195(1)(b) CrPC. The Court did not rely on an earlier case for this determination; it declined to enter into the allegations because the underlying quashing petition remained pending and the alleged suppression would not have affected the interim order.

predicates.suppression_action_application_filed: A party has applied for action alleging that another party suppressed documents or facts in court proceedings.
predicates.underlying_quashing_petition_unresolved: The request to quash the underlying criminal proceedings remains undecided.
predicates.alleged_suppression_would_not_affect_int: The alleged omitted material would not have changed the basis of the interim order under consideration.

issues.definition: A suppression application is disposed of without deciding its merits when the underlying quashing petition remains unresolved and the alleged suppression would not affect the interim order.
